newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF expects stern measures vs Yamaichi--Mitsuzuka.
newsitem.headline: MOF expects stern measures vs Yamaichi--Mitsuzuka.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said that he expects authorities to take stern measures against Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd after the completion of investigations that started on Wednesday.

The fact that Tokyo prosecutors and the Securities Exchange and Surveillance Commission (SESC) conducted searches at Yamaichi's headquarters on Wednesday is extremely regrettable, he told a news conference.
"I want stern measures by the authorities in order to regain public confidence in the securities market," he said.

Mitsuzuka also said that problems at individual companies such as Nomura Securities Co Ltd and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank (DKB), now at the heart of a racketeer payoff scandal, must not affect Japan's efforts to carry out its so-called "Big Bang" financial reforms.
MOF earlier on Wednesday announced punitive measures against Nomura and DKB.
"Problems at individual firms should not be a matter that affects Japan's 'Big Bang' reforms," he said.
"In carrying out the 'Big Bang' reforms, it is important to establish rules and a system for punishment in order to develop trustworthy markets," he added.
